I am writing this to warn you regarding a situation I recently experienced at Mundo Animal. It says it's an outlet. It more appropriately should be called a 'factory'.

Never have I purchased a pet.  At 63 years old, I now remember why.

I have always had animals and volunteered extensively in shelters around the world and under pretty rough conditions.

Although the sales woman was helpful; in fact charming; she even provided a page explaining exactly what I needed to do.  Which I did.  I was surprised and simply heartbroken when I returned four days later. Yes  just four days later, he died.     Her demeanor changed dramatically.

I did not go back to get another bird, nor did I demand to be reimbursed.  I did, explain that since, I did an online search.  Prices for the parrots at Mundo Animal Outlet are roughly four times higher than in other Lisbon stores. Careful; they are also on OLX however not under the same company name.
That same employee stated that 'this had never happened before'? None of their animals had ever died..really? That's difficult to believe.

That same tiny box in which several of these baby birds are 'stored' is kept under the counter. They grow fast. Mixed in the same overheated box are birds of different species in what smelled to be highly unsanitary conditions.  As these birds are young  it is necessary to keep them warm however, several of them were attempting to use their wings and crawling over the others.

I am therefore warning others to steer clear of this place.

Today I called the store twice, once to ask if they had completely yellow male cockatiels and if they were open and what their hours were.
They replied that they had cockatiels, but did not specify how many (I had already called before and they even asked me if they were domesticated or wild because they had different prices, but that they had quite a few). As for the hours, the employee didn't know because the manager wasn't there and she didn't know. I asked them to call me to inform me of the hours, which they assured me they would do, but I only found out the hours because I called them myself. They said they would be open until 7 pm. I reiterated that I wanted a completely yellow male cockatiel. They confirmed this and I thanked them.

I went to the store, I live in Sesimbra, and when I arrived I was attended to by a child who clearly didn't know what they were doing. The manager came and told me that they didn't have any male yellow cockatiels, that the door was open, implying that they had sold all the ones they had during the time I called and the time I went to the store. The manager, who didn't identify herself, must have thought she was talking to a beginner. She showed me more than 6 to 8 animals in a tiny box, which I find outrageous. In addition, at the entrance on the right side there is a normal cage with more than 6 Ringnecks. The lady in question, in a mocking tone, asked me if they were yellow or lutino?
And then she justified herself by saying that her colleague was new and didn't know the difference between wild and domesticated birds. I believe there is a lot of lack of training, but not being able to tell if they have yellow cockatiels?
I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS STORE TO ANYONE
I will ask the authorities to visit your store to see if everything is in order.

I purchased a one-month-old mini lop-eared rabbit from Mundo Animal Outlet on April 14th as a gift for my daughter. The animal passed away on April 17th, just three days after the purchase.

From the moment it arrived home, I followed all the instructions provided by the store regarding feeding, care, and administration of the dewormer, which was delivered in syringes without product identification in a transparent bag with small paw print drawings.

The day after administering the dewormer, the rabbit began to have looser stools and, on April 17th, it passed away.

I tried to contact them by email and have received no response.

I contacted the store again (today, April 21st) to report the situation and was informed that the responsibility would be mine, without any technical explanation. During the call, I felt disrespected; the call was disconnected mid-conversation, and they stopped answering my calls.

I am leaving this testimony to document my experience and await a formal resolution from the company.

Completely unethical and without compassion for these lives, and after seeing some responses given to very accurate criticisms of this same place, I was even more terrified. It immediately made clear the lack of care they have, as they also demonstrate it with customers and the messages that convey the truth about this very precarious behavior.

Be aware before coming here, it's better not to come at all, to see if they leave this store and stop torturing the poor little animals who only deserve love and not blame for the human cruelty to which they are subjected.

WARNING! Lack of ethics and negligence regarding animal health.
I recently bought a baby rabbit from this store and, unfortunately, the experience was devastating. A few days after arriving home, the animal began to show severe signs of respiratory illness. Despite all efforts and veterinary care, it did not survive.
What shocks me most is realizing, through other reports here, that Yuki was not an isolated case. There seems to be a pattern of negligence in the provenance or basic health care of these animals before they are sold. It is unacceptable for a store to treat living beings as disposable merchandise, delivering already sick animals to families who, in a short time, end up dealing with the trauma of loss.
I write this as a warning to everyone who is thinking of acquiring an animal here: be very careful. And to the store management: animals deserve dignity and real care, not just a price tag.
The suffering they caused is irreparable.

I simply did my shopping at the supermarket, walked through the aisles as they were closing, and observed the deplorable state of the animals inside the store, all crammed together, without food and without a kennel to shelter them, and I published my opinion.

On Saturday night when the center closes, and only reopens on Monday, the food bowl was completely empty at that time (the lady from the other store even took a picture). Therefore, the animals went all Saturday night, all of Sunday, and Monday morning until the store opened without eating.
This is a serious violation of animal rights.
Your Excellencies, without knowledge of the facts, offended me, used derogatory terms, made false accusations, and even associated me with a third person I don't know. There are many people with the same surname, and in Portugal, the name Fernandes corresponds to approximately 119,777,000 people with that surname.
Furthermore, it will be very easy to verify in court, through the images, that I have nothing to do with the people you describe.
